fine_trace.note: An attacker-controlled 60-byte AR member header is read from the input file into ar_header; the 10-byte size field at bytes 48..57 is fully attacker-controlled.
size is parsed from the untrusted header field with toInt() and no non-negative validation; a crafted field such as "-1" flows into size as a negative qint64.

Root cause: the allocation size is derived from the unvalidated negative size. For size == -1, new char[0] yields a 0-byte heap buffer that the subsequent unchecked write index overruns. Upstream fix D21149 added 'if (size < 0)' after parsing size.
Sink: with size == -1, ar_longnames[size] writes one byte before the 0-byte heap allocation, a heap-buffer-overflow write (invalid memory access).

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: KAr::openArchive parses the 10-byte size field of each AR member header with toInt() without checking that it is non-negative. A broken .ar file whose longfilename-table ('//') entry declares size -1 makes 'new char[size + 1]' allocate a 0-byte buffer and 'ar_longnames[size] = \0' write before that buffer, a heap-buffer-overflow. This matches the fix commit 'KAr::openArchive: Protect against Heap-buffer-overflow in broken files' (D21149) whose parent is the vulnerable revision: it adds 'if (size < 0) { setErrorString(...); delete[] ar_longnames; return false; }' right after parsing size.
